include: the third pass challenged this author ruling and the challenge holds. All four conditions are met on the abstract's own text — 12 healthy women, acute oral ingestion of the food itself (90 g wild watermelon extract juice), and blood flow in the posterior tibial artery significantly increased against placebo in a randomised double-blind crossover. The bed is an extremity one, which §2.3 names among the beds peripheral circulation reaches ('forearm / calf / hand / foot flow') and whose rationale calls the substrate of felt warmth; the organ-specific carve-out does not apply. The earlier sweep ruling cited the reactivity-probe rule, but none of its named triggers is present: flow was measured supine at 30/60/90 min with no occlusion, no pharmacological probe and no flow-mediated dilatation. Of the 39 limb- or skin-bed records the sweep excluded, every other one carries either an organ or skeletal-muscle bed or a named probe, so this correction removes an inconsistency rather than creating one. The paper's own framing is arterial stiffness and nitric oxide rather than thermal, but §2.3 makes the bed and the probe decisive, not the framing, and amending that rule after seeing which record it decides is the failure this protocol exists to prevent.
no-thermal: the endpoint is heart-rate variability; resting energy expenditure did not differ and is not framed as thermogenesis (§2.3 energy-expenditure qualifier)
